about: A conformance corpus in one shape, for an implementation in any language. Each `validate` case gives an `input` and the `expect` your implementation must produce for it. `valid` means NO ERRORS — a document that draws only warnings is valid, and an implementation that refuses one has confused advice with a rule. The refusals are the substance: any implementation accepts a valid document, and agreeing about what must be refused is where interoperability lives. Generated by tools/conformance-bundle.mjs — regenerated, never hand-edited.

protocol.about: One JSON object per line in, one per line out — so a runner needs no bindings and works with any executable.

stdin.context: optional — present only where the profile judges a document against something else

stdout.codes: string[] — optional; compared only when the case expects them

cases.why: The canonical door: a general lane that asks nothing and a partnership lane that will not act below rung 1, over a ladder that publishes rungs 0 and 1.

input.notAuthority: A rung buys a reply and a place in a queue. It never buys authority, money, or access. Publishing a file at a domain proves that someone can write to that host — it does not prove an organisation is who it says it is, and this door does not treat it as though it did. Where real authority is needed it is delegated and verified through flashyID, and the chain is checked.
